ownership_reason: Only the gold builds the tree, and only the gold sees the token buffer that the value is written into: the buffer is created, given the mapper as its codec, filled and read inside the gold, so no caller can supply or change its codec. Without the codec, a nested value that a serializer writes with writeObject is kept as a raw embedded object and becomes a POJONode in the tree, where the mapper's JSON for the value has an object; which values are affected is decided during serialization, so no caller can decide the case before the call. Hop 1 only translates exceptions (I/O exceptions as IllegalArgumentException, the value converted as it is) and hops 2 to 4 pass the mapper and the value along unchanged, as their javadoc states. The gold's javadoc and the facade's ('construct equivalent JSON Tree representation') state the contract the variant violates on the trigger input. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the intact ObjectMapper._convert (used by every convertValue overload) serializes into new TokenBuffer(this, false), a buffer carrying the mapper as codec; MappingJsonFactory gives its generators a mapper as codec; TestGeneratorUsingMapper::testPojoWriting (a POJO written by a generator with the mapper as codec gives {"x":4}) and testPojoWritingFailing (no codec, no serialization of the POJO) pass, and TestConversions::testConversionOfTrees and testBeanToTree pass through the chain.
